mechanism_fit: M12, same-file competition. The gold, StrTokenizer::readNextToken, and three correct competitors (readWithQuotes, addToken, tokenize) all live in src/main/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/text/StrTokenizer.java (1114 lines), and the trigger executes all four (G6 confirmed this with markers). The trigger observes only public behaviour: getTSVInstance(" one \t\t three\n").getTokenArray() loses the empty middle field ({one,three}). That symptom fits several methods. addToken is the method that drops empty tokens when ignoreEmptyTokens is set. readWithQuotes consumes delimiters and returns the next position, so it could be skipping a second tab. tokenize has its own empty-token logic. The real cause is a quiet operator change in readNextToken's whitespace-skip loop: '||' became '&&'. After the change the loop stops only when a character is both a delimiter and a quote. With TSV, the tab delimiter is also matched by the trim matcher, so the second tab is skipped as whitespace and readNextToken's own empty-token branch is never reached. No file search is needed; the task is purely about which method in the file is responsible.
ownership_reason:
readNextToken owns the fault. The pristine comment directly above its leading loop says the loop skips ignored or trimmed characters 'unless it is the field delimiter or the quote character'. So the loop must stop as soon as either the delimiter matcher or the quote matcher matches. In the variant it stops only when a character is both a delimiter and a quote. The TSV prototype's trimmer is StrMatcher.trimMatcher, and TrimMatcher.isMatch matches every char <= 32, including the tab delimiter. So after the token 'one', readNextToken consumes the second tab as whitespace and never reaches its own 'handle empty token' branch.

The competitors are correct and unchanged (G11):
- addToken drops an empty token only when ignoreEmptyTokens is true, and the TSV prototype sets it to false.
- readWithQuotes ends a token at the first delimiter and returns the position just after it.
- Together with tokenize, readWithQuotes produces empty tokens for consecutive delimiters whenever the delimiter is not also trimmable or ignorable. The existing passing tests StrTokenizerTest::test7 (consecutive space delimiters give "", "") and StrTokenizerTest::test1 (';' delimiter with trailing empties) show this; both are declared as ownership tests and pass on both the variant and the correct configuration.

Restoring '||' in readNextToken alone makes the trigger pass with the full suite green (G1). None of the five declared one-line edits absorbs the fault (G9): three competitor edits (addToken, readWithQuotes, tokenize) and two changes to the TSV trimmer configuration.

concerns:
1. StrTokenizer.java is 1114 lines: large for Lang, but not StringUtils-sized. If 'large source file' is meant strictly, it is a borderline fit.
2. The pristine comment above the loop states the contract in so many words. Once a model reads readNextToken closely, the mismatch with the code is decisive, so the instance may be easier than intended. The difficulty depends on whether models inspect readNextToken or settle on addToken or readWithQuotes.
3. '||' to '&&' also changes when the loop stops at a quote character. That is only observable when the quote character is itself trimmable or ignorable; the existing suite does not cover it and the trigger does not exercise it.
4. isQuote is not executed by the trigger (no quotes in the input), so it is not declared as a decoy.
5. The trigger input deliberately includes a trailing '\n' so that TSV-configuration edits cannot stand in for the repair. This is a construction choice; the test is still neutral and deterministic.
6. The assertion message (ArrayUtils.toString of the tokens, the same style as the existing StrTokenizerTest tests) shows the surviving tokens, which hints that an empty token was lost rather than which method lost it.
7. Validation ran while other agents' validators were running at the same time. That only slowed it down; there were no timeouts or flaky results (G3b got three byte-identical failures).
